listForms.description:
Returns the forms visible to the current identity (`kind=form`, excluding tables and quick payment forms). A personal token returns the forms the user created and those shared with them; an account token returns every form in the account.
By default sorted by id descending (that is, by creation time descending), and `next` is the id of the first row of the next page; when `sort` is passed, rows are sorted by the given field and `next` becomes `row:<offset>`.
50 per page by default, adjustable with `limit` (max 1000).
- Each row carries `entries_count` (entry count) and `last_entry_created_at` (when the last entry was received), usable with `filters` / `sort`.
- With `include_transactions=true`, forms bound to a payment account carry `transactions` payment statistics.

createForm.description: Creates a form from a list of field definitions and returns the full form structure.

getForm.description:
Returns the form's name, `kind`, `scene`, public URL (`url`), description, field definitions and settings. Each element of `fields` is a single-key object `{ "<api_code>": {...} }`, in field order.
Also answers for a table or a quick payment form token; `kind` says which it is.

createEntryLegacy.description: Legacy alias of `POST /forms/{form_token}/entries`, with identical behavior. New integrations should use the new path.

updateForm.description:
Edits a form partially; also accepts `PUT`. The request body must contain at least one of `name` / `description` / `fields` / `setting` / `field_rules`, otherwise returns 400.
- `fields` is changed incrementally through four kinds of operation, `add` / `remove` / `update` / `update_choices`; fields, choices and api_codes not mentioned are all kept;
  `update[].type` changes a field's type in place, and a change that clears entry data must carry `confirm_data_loss: true`.
- `field_rules` does `add` / `remove` / `update` on rules located by the `index` that `GET /forms/{form_token}/field_rules` returns.
- `setting`, as on create, accepts only whitelisted keys.
Returns the full updated form structure.

deleteForm.description: Moves the form and its entries to the trash, from which the product can restore it; on success, returns the form token.

checkFormFieldData.summary: Check whether fields already hold data
checkFormFieldData.description:
Use before deleting a field or choice: checks in batch whether fields (or single choices of a field) already have submitted entries. Deleting a field or choice that still has entries deletes those entries with it, and they cannot be recovered.
Matches the check the web editor runs before deleting.
- Put every deletion target of one edit in the `checks` of a single call (at most 100, may span several fields); `results` matches `checks` one to one, in order.
- When a target cannot be checked (the field or the `parent_field` column does not exist, or `choice_value` matches nothing of the kind `choice_type` names, or names more than one), its row returns `unavailable` with the reason; the other targets return as usual.
- Returns 400 when `checks` is missing, empty, over 100, not a JSON array, or has an item that is not an object.

previewFormFieldTypeChange.description:
Use before changing a field's type (the field's `type` in PATCH /forms/{form_token}): changes no data, and counts, from the field's current entries, how many would be kept and how many cleared after the conversion; matches the preview the web editor shows before converting.
- Put every conversion of one edit in the `checks` of a single call.
- `supported: false`, or `choice_limit_exceeded: true` when multi-line text becomes a choice field, means the edit itself would be refused.

listEntries.description:
Returns form entries page by page, 50 per page by default, set with `limit` (max 1000). Sorted by serial number ascending by default; `next` is the serial number of the first entry of the next page.
- `filters` / `keyword` trigger a conditional query; `created_at` returns only entries created at or after that time (and sorts by creation time instead);
  in both these cases, and when `sort` is passed, `next` becomes a row offset.
- `fields` returns only the given fields (the serial number is always returned).
- Each entry is keyed by field api_code (a field with api_code_alias set is keyed by its alias); for the value shapes see `EntryData`.

createEntry.description:
Submits one entry keyed by field api_code (or api_code_alias). Unknown keys are ignored; when no valid key remains, returns 400, with `error_description` starting with `Entry attributes cannot be empty` and naming each dropped key (not a field of this form, or a signature / calculated field that cannot be written).
- The form's field display rules and field validation still apply; a validation failure returns 400, and `error_description` is `{ "<api_code>": ["error"] }` serialized as a JSON string.
- Mobile fields skip SMS verification; signature fields and calculated fields cannot be written.
- Returns 403 when the form's entry count has reached the plan limit.
- Attachment fields accept several forms of input; see `EntryInput`.

countEntries.description:
Returns the number of entries matching the filters, without the entries themselves. `filters` / `keyword` are the same as for `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries`; with neither, returns the total entry count of the form.
A cooperator counts only the entries visible to their role.

aggregateEntries.description:
Aggregates whole columns on the server over the entries matching the filters (sum, average, count, percentiles, etc.), optionally grouped by 1 to 2 fields. The response size depends only on the number of metrics and groups, not on the amount of data.
- `filters` / `keyword` work as in the entry list, except that `creator_id`, `serial_number` and association field conditions are not supported.

summarizeEntries.description:
Reads an overall summary of the form's entries in one call: an overview (matching count, added today) plus the distribution or numeric statistics of each analysable field. The response is only a few KB, regardless of the amount of data.
- Each field returns a uniform structure by `kind`: choice fields give each choice's count and share, matrix fields are grouped by question, numbers give min / max / sum / average, dates give earliest / latest, text gives the distinct count.
- By default includes every analysable field (fields whose `analytics.summarisable` is true, plus `created_at`), at most 60; fields beyond that are listed in `omitted_fields`, and `truncated` is true.
- Returns 400 when a field named in `fields` is not analysable or not readable by the caller.
- `filters` / `keyword` are the same as for the entry list, but `creator_id`, `serial_number` and association field conditions are not supported (returns 400).

countFormViewEntries.summary: Count the entries of a view
countFormViewEntries.description:
Same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries/count`, but only over the entries the view's filters select: the view's filters apply first, and `filters` / `keyword` narrow the range further on top of them. The view's columns and sort do not affect the result; a view with no filters is the same as the whole form.
Only views visible to the caller are accessible; otherwise 404 (View cannot be found).

aggregateFormViewEntries.summary: Aggregate the entries of a view
aggregateFormViewEntries.description:
Same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries/aggregate`, but only over the entries the view's filters select: the view's filters apply first, and `filters` / `keyword` narrow the range further on top of them. The view's columns and sort do not affect the result; a view with no filters is the same as the whole form.
Only views visible to the caller are accessible; otherwise 404 (View cannot be found).

summarizeFormViewEntries.summary: Summarize the entries of a view
summarizeFormViewEntries.description:
Same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries/summary`, but only over the entries the view's filters select: the view's filters apply first, and `filters` / `keyword` narrow the range further on top of them. The view's columns and sort do not affect the result; a view with no filters is the same as the whole form.
Only views visible to the caller are accessible; otherwise 404 (View cannot be found).

createEntriesBatch.description:
Submits up to 200 entries at a time. Each entry is validated on its own; valid ones are written in bulk, invalid ones are recorded in `errors` (`index` is the position in the request array).
Returns 201 when at least one succeeds and 422 when all fail; returns 400 when `entries` is empty or has over 200 entries.
Before writing, the entry count limit is checked against the number of entries submitted; over the limit returns 403. A batch write does not trigger the callbacks of a single create, but creates one "import" activity record and backfills calculated fields.

patchEntriesBatch.description:
Partially updates entries in batch by serial number, up to 200 rows at a time. Each row requires `serial_number`; `entry` holds the fields to change (fields not mentioned stay unchanged).
Each row is validated on its own; failed rows are recorded in `failed_rows` (`reason` is `invalid_serial_number` / `invalid_attributes`, etc.).
Returns 200 when at least one row succeeds and 422 when all fail; returns 400 when `entries` is empty or has over 200 rows.
Batch update does not handle the attachment lifecycle, so it **cannot write attachment fields** (including attachment columns inside table fields); update those one entry at a time.

getEntry.description: Returns one entry by serial number. `fields` limits the fields returned.

updateEntryViaPost.description: A POST alias of `PATCH` on the same path, with the same partial-update semantics, for clients that cannot easily send PATCH.

replaceEntry.description:
**Full replace**: writable fields absent from the request body are cleared, and only the values submitted in this request are kept. For a partial update use `PATCH`.
Returns 400 when validation fails, with `error_description` being the JSON string of the field errors.

updateEntry.description:
**Partial update**: only the fields present in the request body change; the rest keep their values. An attachment field is replaced as a whole set: to keep existing files, send back the URLs or attachment ids you read along with the new ones.
Returns 400 when validation fails, with `error_description` being the JSON string of the field errors.

deleteEntry.description: Deletes one entry and records a delete activity. On success returns the serial number of the deleted entry; returns 400 when deletion fails (for example, the form's state does not allow it).

listEntryComments.description: Returns all comments on the entry, oldest first, with their creators, mentioned users and attachments. A caller who is a cooperator needs entry read permission on the form, and the entry must be within their data scope; otherwise returns 400.

createEntryComment.description: Creates a comment on the entry, authored by the caller; content is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace. Returns 400 when content is empty or longer than 2000 characters. Mention a user in content with @[<user_id>] (a 24-character hex user id); the mentioned user must be a cooperator on the form, otherwise returns 400 and no comment is created. parent_id makes the comment a reply; the parent comment must belong to the same entry, otherwise returns 400. This endpoint cannot attach files. A caller who is a cooperator needs entry read permission, and the entry must be within their data scope; otherwise returns 400.

updateEntryComment.summary: Update a comment on an entry
updateEntryComment.description: Changes a comment's content; PUT is accepted too. Only the comment's author can edit it; not even a form admin can edit someone else's comment; otherwise returns 400. content follows the same rules as on create (leading and trailing whitespace stripped, at most 2000 characters, mentioned users must be cooperators); the comment's existing attachments stay unchanged. Returns 404 (comment cannot be found) when the comment does not belong to the entry.

deleteEntryComment.summary: Delete a comment on an entry
deleteEntryComment.description: Deletes a comment. The comment's author, the form's creator, or a cooperator with the admin role can delete it; any other cooperator gets 400. Returns 404 (comment cannot be found) for a comment that is already deleted or does not belong to the entry.

getFormSetting.description:
Returns the form's after-submission settings, collection rules (closing rules, fill frequency), access policy, WeChat restrictions and Webhook settings.
The `weixin` key is returned only when the form has a WeChat Official Account selected (selected_weixin_appid is present).

updateFormSetting.description:
Partially updates the form's settings, writing only the keys present in the request; PUT is accepted too.
- `submission_region_limited` / `submission_regions` are a paid feature and read-only here; to write them, use `setting` on the "Edit a form" endpoint.
- `manually_close_rule`, `by_time_range_close_rule`, `by_entries_close_rule` and `fill_frequency` are nested objects; the server creates or updates them as nested attributes.
- Returns `{ "status": "ok" }` on success; returns 400 when model validation fails, with body `{ "errors": "...", "status": "failed" }` (not the common error shape).

getManuallyCloseRule.summary: Show whether a form is manually closed
getManuallyCloseRule.description: Returns whether the form has been manually closed for collection. Returns `{ "closed": false }` when no manual closing rule has ever been created.

updateManuallyCloseRule.description:
Opens (true) or closes (false) the form for collection manually through `open`; PUT is accepted too.
Creates the manual closing rule when none exists, updates it otherwise. When the manual closed state changes, the server deletes the form's other closing rules (by time, by entry count, etc.).
Returns 400 when the `open` parameter is missing (the response body depends on the server implementation); returns 400 when saving fails, with body `{ "errors": "...", "status": "failed" }`.

updateAccessPolicy.description:
Updates the form's fill frequency limit (fill_frequency); PUT is accepted too.
This endpoint takes only the `fill_frequency` key; for the other access policy keys, use PATCH /forms/{form_token}/setting.
Returns `{ "status": "ok" }` on success; returns 400 when validation fails, with body `{ "errors": "...", "status": "failed" }` (not the common error shape).

createFormWebhook.description:
Sets the form's entry push URL `entry_post_url` and turns on pushing new entries (post_new_entry = true).
The plan must support Webhook; otherwise returns 402 with an empty body.
The server does not check the save result and echoes `entry_post_url` from the settings as is (whether an invalid URL was persisted depends on the server implementation).

deleteFormWebhook.description: Removes `entry_post_url` from the form's settings. Returns 200 with an empty body on success.

listNotificationRules.description: Lists the form's notification rules, newest first, each with whether it can send right now.

createNotificationRule.description:
Creates a notification rule; the body follows the schema of its `approach`. The rule sends for matching entries from then on, using the SMS / email balance, and shows on the form's notification settings page. SMS and WeChat messages are reviewed when they are sent.
- Saving an enabled `schedule_time` rule also schedules the entries already in the form whose send time is still ahead.

getNotificationRule.description: Returns the rule and whether it can send right now.

updateNotificationRule.description:
Changes the rule; the body takes only the keys of the rule's own `approach`, and `approach` itself cannot change.
- Saving an enabled `schedule_time` rule schedules the entries already in the form whose send time is still ahead.

deleteNotificationRule.description: Deletes the rule and cancels what it has scheduled but not yet sent.

listNotificationRuleNotifications.summary: List a notification rule's sending records
listNotificationRuleNotifications.description: Lists the notifications a rule sent, newest first, with a summary of the matching records. Covers the last 180 days, as the form's notification log page does; notifications scheduled for later are not included.

updateFormTheme.description: Partially updates the form's theme: colors, background, header image, typography, form container and submit button.

getExamSetting.description:
Returns an exam form's settings for what is shown after the exam is submitted, the time limit, the pre-exam notice and score range comments.
Only for forms in the exam scene (scene = exam); otherwise returns 400. Returns an empty object `{}` when the form has no exam settings record yet.

updateExamSetting.description: Partially updates an exam form's settings.

getEvaluationSetting.description:
Returns an evaluation form's report display, dimension (indicator) settings and total score range comments.
Only for forms in the evaluation scene (scene = evaluation); otherwise returns 400. Returns an empty object `{}` when the form has no evaluation settings record yet.

updateEvaluationSetting.description:
Partially updates an evaluation form's settings (schema `EvaluationSettingInput`).
- `evaluation_comments` replaces the total score range comments as a whole (an empty array turns them off) and takes effect only when `notice_after_filling_mode`, passed or already saved, is reports / customize. A comment written with conditions in the form editor reads back as `id` + `conditions`; pass it back under that id, where only `comment` / `retry` can change.
- `indicator_setting.indicators` replaces the dimensions as a whole; pass `api_code` back to keep a dimension. A dimension binds visible scorable questions by `field_api_codes` or `field_cids`.

listFieldRules.summary: Show a form's field display rules
listFieldRules.description: Returns the form's effective field display rules (logic jumps). `index` is the 0-based position; field_rules updates and removals in PATCH /forms/{form_token} locate rules by this index.

listExtendedAttributes.description: Returns the "track entry source" extended attributes generated for the form (oldest first), each with the fill link that carries its value.

listFormCooperators.description: Returns the form's cooperators and their role names, including roles inherited from folders; when a user gets roles through several paths, only the nearest one is returned.

copyForm.description:
Copies the form and returns the new form (same shape as GET /forms/{form_token}). The new form's creator is the calling user (the account owner for an account token).
- When the source form allows public copying (can_duplicated_in_public), the caller needs no access to the source form; otherwise a caller without access gets 404.
- Returns 403 when the source form is frozen or its creator's account is disabled, with body `{ "errors": ..., "status_code": "form_forbidden" }` (not the common error shape).
- `folder_token` takes a folder token or id; returns 404 when the folder does not exist or the caller lacks manage permission on it.
- Returns 400 when copying fails (model validation does not pass).

moveFormToFolder.summary: Move a form into a folder
moveFormToFolder.description:
Moves the form into a folder, or out of one (pass null as `folder_token`); PUT is accepted too. The move affects only the calling user's folder placement.
- The request body must contain the `folder_token` key (its value may be null); otherwise 400.
- `folder_token` takes only a folder token (not an id); returns 404 when the folder does not exist or the current user lacks manage permission on it.
- The folder type (form / table) must match the form's type; otherwise 400.
- To move a table, use `PATCH /tables/{table_token}/folder`.

createWeixinOauthSession.summary: Exchange a WeChat authorization code for an openid
createWeixinOauthSession.description:
Exchanges the `code` returned by WeChat web authorization for the user's openid, through the WeChat Official Account the form has selected.
When the form's WeChat authorization scope is userinfo, also returns `unionid` (when WeChat returns one) and `profile`.
- Returns 400 when the form has no WeChat Official Account configured or that account does not exist; returns 400 when `code` is missing.
- Returns 502 when the exchange fails on the WeChat side (invalid code, etc.) or fetching the user info fails.

listFormViews.description: Returns the views the caller can see on the form: views they created, and views whose visibility other cooperators set to cooperators; other users' personal views are not returned. The order follows the caller's own saved view order; views not in it are appended by position, then created_at.

createFormView.summary: Create a view on a form
createFormView.description: Creates a new view on the form, created by the caller; visibility defaults to cooperators when not passed, and position is the highest position among the currently visible views plus 1. Each user can have at most 100 views on one form; at the limit, returns 422 (View limit reached). When view_type is kanban and kanban_group_by_api_code is not passed, the server picks the grouping field; when kanban_hidden_groups is not passed, the __unset__ group is hidden by default; when prefer_columns is empty, the form's default columns are used (at most 5 columns for a kanban view, serial_number included). Returns 422 when filter is invalid (not an array, unknown field, unsupported operator, invalid value). Returns 422 when model validation fails (e.g. name is empty or longer than 120 characters, or the grouping field does not support kanban grouping). Form views (view_type form): supported only on tables, otherwise 422; title defaults to the table name; without field_overrides, all fillable columns are selected in the current column order; published defaults to false (the fill link does not work while unpublished). title / description / published / field_overrides apply only to form views; using them on another type returns 422. Creating, updating or deleting a form view (including switching a view to or from a form view) requires the caller to hold a predefined role on the table that can add entries, otherwise 403; an account token is exempt. Returns 422 when a fill item's column does not exist, cannot be a fill item, or sets a validation its column type does not support; the error message names the column's api_code.

getFormView.summary: Show a view of a form
getFormView.description: Returns one view. Only views visible to the caller can be read (created by the caller or visible to cooperators); another user's personal view returns 404 (View cannot be found).

updateFormView.summary: Update a view of a form
updateFormView.description: Updates the view's configuration; PUT is accepted too. Only the keys present in the request are updated: an empty array for filter clears the filters, and leaving filter out keeps them unchanged; when kanban_group_by_api_code changes and kanban_group_order / kanban_hidden_groups are not passed with it, those two lists reset to their defaults. Cooperators can change the configuration of a view visible to cooperators, but only the view's creator can switch visibility, otherwise returns 403; a view whose view_scope is form cannot switch visibility. Returns 422 when filter is invalid or model validation fails. field_overrides replaces the fill item settings as a whole; form views have the same permission requirements and parameter limits as on create.

deleteFormView.summary: Delete a view of a form
deleteFormView.description: Deletes a view. Predefined views (predefined) and views whose view_scope is form cannot be deleted, and the deletion is also refused when it would leave the caller with no visible view; all of these return 422. Deleting a form view needs the same permission as creating one (otherwise 403); once it is deleted, its fill link stops working immediately, and this cannot be undone.

listFormViewEntries.description: Returns the form's entries under the view's filters and sort rules, at most 50 per page. The returned fields are limited to those in the view's prefer_columns (serial_number always included); when prefer_columns is empty, all pushable fields are returned. Sorting follows the view's sort rules, with serial_number ascending appended when they do not include serial_number. Paginate with the next parameter (a row offset); next is null on the last page. Returns 400 when the view's filters use an operator the query engine does not support. Only views visible to the caller are accessible, otherwise 404 (View cannot be found).

uploadEntryAttachment.description: Uploads a file for an attachment field of the form, or for an attachment column of a table field.

prepareEntryAttachmentUpload.description:
Issues a one-time link for uploading a local file to an attachment field, or to an attachment column of a table field, without sending its bytes in a request body.
- With a shell that can read the file and reach the network, run `curl -F file=@<path> <upload_url>`, then put the returned `attachment_id` in the field when creating or updating an entry.
- Without one, or when curl fails (for example under a sandbox's network limits), send small content as Base64 to "Upload an entry attachment".

uploadImportFile.description: Uploads a spreadsheet (`.xlsx` / `.xls` / `.csv`) for importing entries into the form.

prepareImportFileUpload.description:
Issues a one-time link for uploading a local spreadsheet (`.xlsx` / `.xls` / `.csv`) to import into the form, without sending its bytes in a request body.
- With a shell that can read the file and reach the network, run `curl -F file=@<path> <upload_url>`, then pass the returned `attachment_id` to "Import entries from an uploaded spreadsheet"; read the header row from your local copy.
- Without one, or when curl fails, the file cannot be uploaded: spreadsheets have no Base64 route.

createEntryImport.summary: Import entries from an uploaded spreadsheet
createEntryImport.description:
Appends each row of a spreadsheet uploaded with "Upload an import file" as an entry of this form. Upload the file first to get the import attachment ID (`attachment_id`), then say here which column goes into which field.
Once validation passes, returns `201` and the entries are written in the background: `201` means the job has started, not finished; poll "Show an entry import job" for the result.
- Every required field of the form needs a column, and a field takes at most one column.
- A refused import writes no entries, and its error shows the row and column range and the header of the spreadsheet, so fix the mapping from it and retry.

getEntryImport.description:
Returns the progress and result of an entry import job. While `status` is `pending` / `running`, the job is still in progress, and `processed_rows` and `total_rows` can be used to show progress;
`success` / `failed` / `cancelled` are final states; `imported_count` / `skip_count` / `invalid_count` are the numbers of rows written, skipped and failing validation, `warnings` holds per-row notices, and `error_message` is why the job failed.
A job can be read only through the form it imports into: when the id does not exist, is not a valid id, or belongs to another form, returns 404 `Import job not found for this form — check the id, and that it belongs to this form.`.
Returns 404 `form cannot be found` when the form does not exist or is not accessible to the current caller.

estimateSmsTask.description:
Picks the entries an SMS task would send to and counts the messages it would charge, without sending anything.
- `POST /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks` with the same parameters picks the entries again when it runs, so its count changes if they changed in between.
- A cooperator picks only the entries visible to their role.

listSmsTasks.description: Lists the SMS tasks of this form.

createSmsTask.description:
Creates an SMS task that sends a template message to each entry picked.
- Estimate first with `GET /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks/estimate` and send with the same parameters; the entries are picked again when this runs.
- The task may wait in `template_checking` or `content_auditing` while the template or content is under review, and sends once approved.
- When the estimate's `can_send` is false the task is still created, and when sending finds the quota and balance short it stops, ending `none_sent` or `partial_sent` with the reason in `failed_reason`.
- Sent messages cannot be recalled, and retrying a request that succeeded sends again.

getSmsTask.description: Returns an SMS task of this form with its status and sending progress.

updateSmsTask.summary: Revoke an SMS task, or change one whose template failed review and send it again
updateSmsTask.description:
Revokes an SMS task that has not started sending, or changes a `template_fail` task and sends it again, keeping its `id`.
- `revoked: true` revokes a `waiting_for_send` or `content_auditing` task so it never sends.
- Otherwise the body changes a `template_fail` task, keeping its entries. Estimate first with `GET /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks/{id}/estimate`.
- A changed task goes through review and sending as one created by `POST /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks`; sent messages cannot be recalled.

listSmsTaskActivities.summary: List an SMS task's sending results
listSmsTaskActivities.description: Lists the sending result of each mobile number an SMS task sent to.

estimateSmsTaskResend.description:
Picks the entries that resending an SMS task would send to and counts the messages it would charge, without sending anything.
- The entries are the task's entries with the `status` result in its sending results, narrowed by `filters` / `keyword` / `view_token`; no other entry is ever picked.
- An entry holding several numbers is picked when any of them got that result, and is sent to on all of them.
- `POST /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks/{id}/resend` with the same parameters picks the entries again when it runs, so its count changes if they changed in between.
- A cooperator picks only the entries visible to their role.

resendSmsTask.description:
Sends an SMS task again as a new task, to its entries with a given result in its sending results.
- Estimate first with `GET /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks/{id}/resend/estimate` and send with the same parameters; the entries are picked again when this runs.
- The new task keeps the original's template, `entry_field` and `placeholder_keys` and is sent as by `POST /forms/{form_token}/sms_tasks`; the original task is left unchanged.
- Sent messages cannot be recalled, and retrying a request that succeeded sends again.

estimateSmsTaskChange.summary: Estimate changing an SMS task whose template failed review
estimateSmsTaskChange.description:
Estimates changing a `template_fail` SMS task and sending it again, without changing or sending anything.
- Counts the entries the task holds without reading them: content with variables gives a lower bound (`at_least`), and a table column `entry_field` gives null numbers and cost.

sendSmsTask.summary: Send an SMS task created with auto_send false
sendSmsTask.description: Sends a task created with `auto_send` false once it has passed review, to the entries fixed at creation; a task given `send_at` waits until then.

estimateEmailTask.description:
Picks the entries an email task would send to and checks the quota, without sending anything.
- `POST /forms/{form_token}/email_tasks` with the same parameters picks the entries again when it runs, so its count changes if they changed in between.
- A cooperator picks only the entries visible to their role.

listEmailTasks.description: Lists the email tasks of this form.

createEmailTask.description:
Creates an email task that sends an email to each entry picked, starting right away.
- Estimate first with `GET /forms/{form_token}/email_tasks/estimate` and send with the same parameters; the entries are picked again when this runs.
- When the estimate's `can_send` is false the task is still created, and when sending finds the quota and balance short it stops, ending `none_sent` or `partial_sent` with the reason in `failed_reason`.
- Sent emails cannot be recalled, and retrying a request that succeeded sends again.

getEmailTask.description: Returns an email task of this form with its status and sending progress.

listEmailTaskActivities.summary: List an email task's sending results
listEmailTaskActivities.description: Lists the sending result of each entry an email task sent to.

estimateEmailTaskResend.description:
Picks the entries that resending an email task would send to and checks the quota, without sending anything.
- The entries are the task's entries with the `status` result in its sending results, narrowed by `filters` / `keyword` / `view_token`; no other entry is ever picked.
- The emails go through the task's custom SMTP account, using no quota, while the account can still use it.
- `POST /forms/{form_token}/email_tasks/{id}/resend` with the same parameters picks the entries again when it runs, so its count changes if they changed in between.
- A cooperator picks only the entries visible to their role.

resendEmailTask.description:
Sends an email task again as a new task, to its entries with a given result in its sending results.
- Estimate first with `GET /forms/{form_token}/email_tasks/{id}/resend/estimate` and send with the same parameters; the entries are picked again when this runs.
- The new task keeps the original's `entry_field`, subject, body and custom SMTP account and is sent as by `POST /forms/{form_token}/email_tasks`; the original task is left unchanged.
- Sent emails cannot be recalled, and retrying a request that succeeded sends again.

uploadFormImage.description: Uploads an image for a form; it takes effect once a form, theme or public query references it. - `description` returns a `url` for an `` in the form `description` or a field's `notes`, at most 30 per form; every other type returns an `attachment_id` for the property that names that `image_type`. - An `attachment_id` is taken only where its `image_type` goes, and only while the image is unused or already that form's; an image nothing uses within 7 days is deleted.

prepareFormImageUpload.description:
Issues a one-time link for uploading a local image for a form, without sending its bytes in a request body.
- With a shell that can read the file and reach the network, run `curl -F file=@<path> <upload_url>`, then use the returned `attachment_id` (or `url`) where its `image_type` goes.
- Without one, or when curl fails (for example under a sandbox's network limits), give a public image URL or a small Base64 image where the image goes.

uploadUserLicenseAttachment.description: Uploads a business license or ID card image for `POST /sms/signatures` and `PATCH /sms/signatures/{id}`; only the uploader can use it.

listTables.description: Returns the tables (`kind=table`) visible to the current caller. Pagination, `q`, `filters`, `sort`, `next`, `skip` and `limit` mean the same as in the form list; 50 per page by default, up to 1000.

getTable.description: Returns the table's basic information, field definitions and the views visible to the current caller. Returns 404 `table cannot be found` when the token is not a table (for example, a regular form).

updateTable.description: Edits a table incrementally; `PUT` is also accepted. The request body is the same as for editing a form (`kind` is ignored); attachment columns in `fields.add` and `fields.update` do not accept limit properties, and types in `fields.add` must be column types tables support.

deleteTable.description: Deletes a table and its entries; on success, returns the table token.

checkTableFieldData.summary: Check whether table columns already hold data
checkTableFieldData.description: Same as GET /forms/{form_token}/fields/check, applied to the columns of a table. Returns 404 (`table cannot be found`) when `table_token` does not point to a table.

previewTableFieldTypeChange.summary: Preview a table column type change
previewTableFieldTypeChange.description:
Same as GET /forms/{form_token}/fields/preview_convert, applied to the columns of a table; `target_type` accepts only column types tables support (see `GET /field_types?kind=table`).
Returns 404 (`table cannot be found`) when `table_token` does not point to a table.

listTableEntries.description: Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).

countTableEntries.description: Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries/count`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).

aggregateTableEntries.description:
Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries/aggregate`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).
For the functions and groupings each field supports, see `GET /tables/{table_token}?include_analytics=true`.

summarizeTableEntries.description: Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/entries/summary`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).

countTableViewEntries.summary: Count the entries of a view
countTableViewEntries.description: Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/views/{view_token}/entries/count`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).

aggregateTableViewEntries.summary: Aggregate the entries of a view
aggregateTableViewEntries.description: Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/views/{view_token}/entries/aggregate`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).

summarizeTableViewEntries.summary: Summarize the entries of a view
summarizeTableViewEntries.description: Exactly the same as `GET /forms/{form_token}/views/{view_token}/entries/summary`, except that the target must be a table (otherwise 404 `table cannot be found`).

updateTableEntryViaPost.description: A POST alias for `PATCH` on the same path; it performs an incremental update.

listTableEntryComments.description: Returns all comments on this table entry in ascending order of creation time, under the same rules as form entry comments. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

createTableEntryComment.description: Creates a comment on this table entry, with the same parameters and limits as form entry comments (content is required, at most 2000 characters, mentioned users must be cooperators, parent_id must belong to the same entry). Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

updateTableEntryComment.summary: Update a comment on a table entry
updateTableEntryComment.description: Changes the content of a table entry comment; PUT is also accepted. Only the comment's author can edit it, otherwise returns 400; returns 404 when the comment does not belong to this entry. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

deleteTableEntryComment.summary: Delete a comment on a table entry
deleteTableEntryComment.description: Deletes a table entry comment. The comment's author, the table's creator, or a cooperator with the admin role can delete it; other cooperators get 400; a comment already deleted returns 404. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

listTableViews.description: Returns the views of this table visible to the current caller, under the same rules as listing form views. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table (kind is not table).

createTableView.summary: Create a view on a table
createTableView.description: Creates a view on a table, with the same parameters and limits as creating a form view (at most 100 views per user per table, name at most 120 characters, an invalid filter returns 422). Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table. view_type can be form (a form view, a public fill page); see creating a form view for the rules.

getTableView.summary: Show a view of a table
getTableView.description: Returns one table view; only views visible to the caller can be read. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

updateTableView.summary: Update a view of a table
updateTableView.description: Updates a table view's settings; PUT is also accepted. The rules are the same as for updating a form view: only the creator can change visibility (otherwise 403), and a filter or model validation failure returns 422. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

deleteTableView.summary: Delete a view of a table
deleteTableView.description: Deletes a table view. Predefined views, views whose view_scope is form, and the caller's last visible view cannot be deleted; these return 422. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table. Deleting a form view requires a predefined role that can add entries (otherwise 403); once deleted, its fill link stops working immediately, and this cannot be undone.

listTableViewEntries.description: Returns entries using the table view's filters and sort, at most 50 per page; pagination and the rules for which fields are returned are the same as for form view entries. Returns 404 (table cannot be found) when the token is not a table.

listCheckinCampaigns.description: Lists the check-in campaigns the caller created, newest first. With an account-level credential, returns the ones the account owner created.

createCheckinCampaign.description:
Turns check-in on for a form.
- Refused while the after-submit step of the form is taken by something else (WeChat red envelope, lucky wheel, certificate, confirmation code, another plugin or the check-in code of another campaign, or an after-submit action other than the default message); the message names it, so turn that off first.
- Only one check-in campaign is in effect on a form at a time; creating one turns off the one that was in effect.

getCheckinCampaign.description: Returns the campaign's settings, how many have checked in, and its check-in, verifier invite and management links. Only campaigns the caller created.

updateCheckinCampaign.description:
Updates only the keys present in the body; PUT is accepted too. Only campaigns the caller created.
Turning it back on with `enabled: true` turns off any other campaign in effect on the form.

deleteCheckinCampaign.description: Deletes the campaign and unbinds it from the form; its check-in records are no longer visible. To pause check-in only, PATCH `enabled: false`.

listOpensearchQueries.description: Returns the public queries created by the current caller (an account access token counts as the account owner), newest first, with summary fields only. With form_token, returns only the queries under that form; returns 404 when form_token does not exist or the caller cannot access it, instead of ignoring the parameter.

createOpensearchQuery.description: Creates a public query on the form given by form_token, with the current caller as its creator. The caller must be able to manage the form: no access returns 404, read but not manage returns 403; a plan without the public query feature returns 402. Fields referenced in search_field_rules must be searchable fields of the form, and those in display_field_rules must be displayable fields; otherwise returns 400 listing the available api_code values. search_field_rules / display_field_rules, when passed, cannot be empty arrays; scope_conditions requires a plan that supports limiting the range of searchable entries. A preview image is generated asynchronously after saving.

getOpensearchQuery.description: Returns the public query details, including the search field rules and display field rules. The caller can read only queries it created; another user's query returns 404 (opensearch query cannot be found).

updateOpensearchQuery.description: Updates a public query the caller created; PUT is also accepted. Only the keys present in the request are updated. Returns 400 when the query's form has been deleted. Field rules are validated as on create: referencing a field that cannot be searched / displayed, an empty rule array, an empty name and the like all return 400. An update does not check form manage permission or whether the plan includes public queries.

listOpensearchQuerySuggestions.summary: Suggest fields for a public query
listOpensearchQuerySuggestions.description: Returns the search fields and display fields a form offers for public queries, plus the recommended field api_code values, for building search_field_rules / display_field_rules. The caller must be able to manage the form: no access returns 404, read but not manage returns 403. Whether the plan includes public queries is not checked.

listFolders.description:
Lists the folders the current user has manage permission on (form folders and table folders alike, told apart by `kind`), newest first. With an account-level credential, returns the account owner's folders.
`limit` defaults to 50 and is clamped to 1 to 100; there is no paging: `total` is the full count, `count` the number returned this time.

createFolder.description:
Creates a folder as the current user; the creator becomes the folder's manager. `kind` decides whether the folder holds forms (`form`, the default) or tables (`table`).
Returns 400 `Name cannot be empty` when `name` is empty; returns 400 `Kind must be one of: form, table` when `kind` is not form / table; returns 400 when model validation fails, with the validation message in `error_description`.

getFolder.description: Returns one folder the current user can manage.

listPredefinedChoicesSets.description: Lists the current account's custom predefined choice sets (type custom), only those matching the locale of the current request (as the server implements it); the built-in global choice sets are not returned.

createPredefinedChoicesSet.description:
Creates a custom predefined choice set in the current account. It looks up by `label`: when the account already has a set with the same label, that set's `choices` are overwritten (in effect an update); otherwise a new set is created.
The request body must be wrapped under the `predefined_choices_set` key; returns 400 when the key is missing. Empty strings in `choices` are dropped; neither `label` nor the remaining `choices` may be empty, otherwise returns 400 with the body `{ errors, status: "failed" }`.
Returns 200 on success (not 201).

updatePredefinedChoicesSet.description:
Updates the `label` and / or `choices` of one of the current account's custom predefined choice sets. PUT is also accepted and behaves the same.
Only a set of type custom that belongs to the current account can be updated: a global set or another account's set returns 403 `{ errors: "forbidden", status: "failed" }`; an ID that does not exist returns 404 `{ errors: "not found", status: "failed" }`; a validation failure returns 400 `{ errors, status: "failed" }`.

deletePredefinedChoicesSet.description:
Deletes one of the current account's custom predefined choice sets; returns 200 with no response body on success.
Only a set of type custom that belongs to the current account can be deleted: a global set or another account's set returns 403 `{ errors: "forbidden", status: "failed" }`; an ID that does not exist returns 404 `{ errors: "not found", status: "failed" }`.

createTemplateUsage.summary: Create a form from a template
createTemplateUsage.description:
Uses a template from the template market as the current user, copies it into a new form, and returns the new form's token and edit page URL.
The template is given by `id` (or `template_id`), which takes a template token or a 24-character hexadecimal ID. Optional parameters: `tags` (tags, an array or a comma-separated string), `tag_id` / `folder_id` (the tag / folder the new form goes into), `scene` (target scene; falls back to form when the template has fields the scene does not allow), `frm` (source marker; affects the recorded created_from), `create_source`, `group_id`.
Payment-related branches:
- Paid template the current user has not bought: returns 200 with the body `{ template_url }` (the template purchase page URL), and no form is created.
- Template uses paid features the current plan does not offer: returns 403 `{ error: "CAN_FEATURE_TRIAL", target_plan, target_trial_type, ... }` when the caller is an admin and a feature trial can be started; otherwise returns 403 `{ error: "PAID_FEATURE_REQUIRED", target_plan, template_url }`; an account from a channel partner gets 403 `{ error: "UNAVAILABLE_TO_TRIAL_OR_UPGRADE" }`.
- With `form_app_trial_alert` passed and the template bound to form apps that must be bought / tried: returns 200 `{ error: "CANNOT_FORM_APP_TRIAL" | "FORM_APP_TRIAL_REQUIRED", ... }`; confirm with `confirm_unbind_form_app` / `confirm_form_app_trial` and retry.
When form creation fails (failing the content risk check included), returns 400 `{ error }`. When the template does not exist, returns 404 with an HTML page, not JSON.
`mobile_editor_forbidden` appears only on a mobile request when the new form has the card layout and the current plan cannot use the mobile editor.

listContacts.description:
Lists the current user's contacts page by page, by ID descending, a fixed 50 per page. With an account-level credential, returns the account owner's contacts.
Cursor paging: `next` in the response is the ID of the first contact on the next page; pass it as the query parameter `next` to get that page. `next` is null when there is no more data.

getCurrentUser.description: Returns the user behind the current credential. With an account-level credential (no specific user), returns the account owner.

getBillingAccount.description:
Returns the account the current credential belongs to: plan, this month's usage and quota, feature trial status, and the bound payment merchant / WeChat Pay / Alipay accounts.
`usage` is null when the account has no usage record for this month yet.

listBillingAccountUsers.description:
Lists the members of the current account (deactivated members included), by status ascending (active first), then by creation time, newest first.
`limit` defaults to 50 and is clamped to 1 to 100; there is no paging: `total` is the total number of members, `count` the number returned this time.

listBillingAccountInvoices.description:
Lists the e-invoices the current account has requested (newest request first, all at once, no paging), and the spending that can be invoiced but has not been yet.
Only an account admin can read it: a non-admin member gets 403 (`Only an account admin can read this.`); an account-level credential (no specific user) is treated as the account owner.

listBillingAccountPaymentHistories.description:
Lists the current account's top-ups and spending on Jinshuju (account balance transactions such as buying plans, SMS, AI points and attachment storage), newest first.
This is what the account itself spent; money received through payment forms is not included.
Only an account admin can read it: a non-admin member gets 403 (`Only an account admin can read this.`); an account-level credential (no specific user) is treated as the account owner.
There is no paging: `limit` defaults to 50 and is clamped to 1 to 1000; `total_records` is the number of matching records, `returned_records` the number returned this time.
With `include_balance=true`, `current_balance` is included (account balance and the remaining quota of each item); when records are returned, `statistics` is included (counting only the returned records).

listBillingAccountPaidFeatures.summary: List the paid features and whether the account has each
listBillingAccountPaidFeatures.description: Lists every paid feature with its Chinese name and whether the account has it now; one bought or granted on its own counts. Quotas, and whether each add-on service can still be used, are in `usage` of `GET /billing_account`.

getTradeMerchant.description:
Returns the current account's 小金商户 (the merchant Jinshuju collects payments for) and its onboarding progress: merchant profile, legal entity and contact details, balance, settlement details, payment channel authorization, freeze status, bound payment forms, and the URL for the next step.
- An account without a 小金商户 still gets 200, with `merchant_stage` saying how far onboarding has got; an account that collects payments through its own WeChat Pay / Alipay merchant (direct connection) has no rate, settlement account, balance or onboarding status on Jinshuju.
- `balance` is null when the balance lookup failed, which does not mean the balance is 0.

listTradeTransactions.description:
Lists the payment orders of the 小金商户 (orders customers place by paying on payment forms), filtered and sorted newest first by order time. Only 小金商户 orders are included: orders collected through a direct connection, simulated-payment orders, and unpaid quick payment records are all left out.
- Without dates, covers the last 90 days.
- Records are returned only for a range of at most 90 days with at most 200 matching orders: past either, `transactions` is null, `detail_limit` says why, and `stats` still covers the range; narrow the range to get the records.

aggregateTradeTransactions.description:
Totals the transaction amount, paid count and order count of the 小金商户 payment orders over a date range, optionally grouped by one dimension. Orders are counted as in "List payment orders" (only 小金商户 orders; no simulated payments and no unpaid quick payment records); the totals cover the whole range and are not bound by the detail limits.
- The date range filters on order time, in Beijing time (UTC+8); both ends are inclusive and must be passed together. Without them, it defaults to the last 30 days. The range spans at most 366 days; a longer one returns 400.
- `transactions_amount` (transaction amount): the amount of paid-type orders minus each order's successful refunds, counted on the day the order was placed; refunded and unpaid orders contribute 0. `transactions_count` (paid count): the number of paid, partially refunded and refunding orders. `orders_count` (order count): the number of all matching orders, unpaid included.
- `group_by=time` groups by time: by day for a range under 90 days, by week from 90 days, by month from 365 days; `granularity` gives the granularity, and periods without orders are filled with zero. `paid_status` / `payment_channel` make one group per value; the group whose `payment_channel` is null holds orders that have not started payment. Under the same filters, the groups add up to the total.
- Returns 404 when the account has no 小金商户.

listTradeRefunds.description:
Lists the refunds the 小金商户 issued to customers, with statistics. Refunds are filtered and sorted newest first by the time they were issued, not by the order time or the time the refund arrived.
- Without dates, covers the last 90 days.
- Records are returned only for a range of at most 90 days with at most 200 matching refunds: past either, `refunds` is null, `detail_limit` says why, and `stats` still covers the range.

listTradePayouts.description:
Lists the payouts the 小金商户 made from its Jinshuju balance to its own bank account, with statistics. Payouts are filtered and sorted newest first by request time.
- Without dates, covers the last 90 days.
- Records are returned only for a range of at most 90 days with at most 200 matching payouts: past either, `payouts` is null, `detail_limit` says why, and `stats` still covers the range.

listSmsAuditStatuses.description:
Lists the SMS signatures the current user applied for and the SMS templates under each signature, with review status and the reason a review failed, newest signature first.
Returns only the current user's own signatures, not those of other members of the account; with an account-level credential, returns the account owner's signatures. Any member can call it; admin is not required.

listSmsSignatures.description: Lists the account's SMS signatures, newest first. Pagination as in the form list; 50 per page by default, up to 1000.

createSmsSignature.description:
Applies for an SMS signature and submits it for review; follow the result with `GET /sms/signatures`.
- Upload the images with `POST /user/license_attachments` first.
- A signature the account already has under review or approved is returned unchanged.
- The materials replace the user's ID card information, and the account's business license unless the account has passed license verification.

updateSmsSignature.description:
Changes a rejected signature of the account and submits it for review again.
- After a text change, its templates stay under the old text until each is updated with `PATCH /sms/templates/{id}`.
- The materials replace the user's ID card information, and the account's business license unless the account has passed license verification.

deleteSmsSignature.description: Deletes a rejected signature of the account together with all its templates, including other members' ones.

listSmsTemplates.description: Lists the templates the current user created and the ones other members share, newest first. Pagination as in the form list; 50 per page by default, up to 1000.

createSmsTemplate.summary: Submit an SMS template for review
createSmsTemplate.description: Submits an SMS template for review under a notification signature the account has applied for, even one still under review; follow the result with `GET /sms/templates`.

updateSmsTemplate.description: Changes a template the current user created and submits it for review again; an approved one cannot be sent until approved again.

deleteSmsTemplate.description: Deletes a template the current user created; notifications that send it stop sending SMS.

listSmtpAccounts.description:
Lists the verified custom SMTP accounts the account can send email through.
- The list is empty when the plan does not include custom SMTP.
- Every member gets the same list; admin is not required.

verifyRedirectParams.description:
Lets the receiver of a "redirect to an external URL after submission" verify that the redirect parameters have not been tampered with. This endpoint needs no API credentials.
When a form has redirect after submission turned on and "Fields to carry on redirect" configured, Jinshuju appends the values of the selected fields to the redirect URL, plus the signature parameter `jamr_h` (signed over the form token, the entry token and a 10-minute validity period). The receiver forwards the received `jamr_h` and all field parameters to this endpoint unchanged: the server verifies the signature, finds the form and entry, and compares the current value of each configured field with the passed parameter value (array values must be equal as a whole; other values are compared as strings).
Returns 200 `{ status: "SUCCESS", message: "验证成功" }` when all match; 400 `{ status: "FAIL", message: "无效Token或者过期" }` when the `jamr_h` signature is invalid or expired; 400 `{ status: "FAIL", message: "验证失败" }` when the form / entry does not exist, a field value does not match, or a field parameter is missing. The message text follows the request language.

listFieldTypes.description:
Returns every field type available when creating / editing a form (or table), with the validation switches and type-specific settings each type accepts, for building `type` and the type-specific parameters in `fields`.
Kept in line with the types and parameters the create endpoints actually accept.

getFieldType.description:
Returns the validation switches and type-specific settings one field type accepts, shaped like one item of the `GET /field_types` list.
Returns 404, listing the available types in `error_description`, when the type name does not exist or is not among the types available for `kind` (e.g. querying a type tables do not support with `kind=table`).

countEntriesAcrossForms.description:
Counts, in one call, the entries matching the filters in each of up to 10 forms / tables, plus their total.
- A token that cannot be accessed (does not exist, or does not belong to the caller) does not fail the whole request; its row returns `unavailable` with the reason instead. The total adds up only the rows that could be counted.
- Field api_codes mean different things in each form, so `filters` can use only the three form-independent conditions `created_at` / `updated_at` / `creator_id`; any other field returns 400.
- `keyword` is not supported (passing it returns 400); to search several forms by keyword, use `GET /entries/search`.

searchEntriesAcrossForms.description:
Runs one keyword as a full-text search across several forms / tables and returns, per form, the match count and some of the matching serial numbers (at most 50 per form), without entry content.
- Search scope: the forms in `form_tokens` when given; otherwise every form and table the caller can access (for an account access token, every form and table in the account).
  Either way, `filters` then narrows the scope; unless `filters` specifies `entries_count`, only forms with entries are searched by default (`entries_count > 0`).
- The scope holds at most 10 forms; beyond that it returns 400: narrow it with `filters`, or pass `form_tokens` directly.
- Forms with no match are left out of the result; forms that cannot be accessed, where the caller's role does not allow reading entries, whose search timed out or whose search service did not respond are listed with `unavailable` giving the reason (this does not mean there was no match).

getEntryStats.summary: Count submissions per form over a date range
getEntryStats.description:
Counts the submissions received within a date range by every form / table the caller can access (for an account access token, every form and table in the account): returns the total, and a list of the forms that received submissions, most submissions first.
- Dates are in Beijing time (UTC+8); `from` / `to` are both inclusive.
- It counts submissions as they happened: imported entries count on the day of the import, and deleted entries are not subtracted, so the result may differ from a count by entry `created_at`.
- The list has at most `limit` rows; when there are more, `truncated` is true, and `total` and `forms_with_data` still cover every form.
- With `by` (`day` / `week` / `month`), the response also carries `buckets`: one count of the same shape for each period in the range (periods with no submissions included); weeks start on Monday, and the first and last periods are clipped to the range. The range covers at most 92 days / 53 weeks / 24 months; beyond that it returns 400, suggesting a coarser granularity or dropping `by`.

listMyFilledForms.summary: List the forms I have submitted to
listMyFilledForms.description:
Returns the forms the current user has submitted entries to as a submitter (quick payment forms excluded), most recent submission first. These forms need not be created by or shared with the current user;
each row gives the current user's own submission count and latest submission time, not the form's total entry count. Deleted forms do not appear in `data` (`total` still counts them).
- Pagination: `next` is a row offset, passed back as is for the next page; `skip` and `next` cannot be combined. 50 rows per page by default, adjustable with `limit` (at most 1000).
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

listMySubmittedEntries.summary: List my entries in a form
listMySubmittedEntries.description:
Returns the entries the current user submitted to the given form, newest first. The form need not be created by or shared with the current user: only the user's own entries are returned,
with only the fields the form makes public to submitters (hidden fields are neither returned nor usable for filtering or searching).
- `filters` works as in the entry list, but cannot use `creator_id`, since results are already the user's own.
- `keyword` is not subject to the form's entry-count limit.
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

searchMySubmittedEntries.description:
Searches the current user's own entries in every form they submitted to (quick payment forms excluded) with one keyword, over the fields each form makes public to submitters, and returns the match count and serial numbers for each matching form.
- One call searches at most 20 forms; past that, name the ones to search in `form_tokens`.
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

getFillFormPage.description:
Reads the fill page behind a fill link (`/f/<token>`): its title, description, the fields to fill in, and whether the current user can submit right now.
The caller reads it as a submitter holding the link and needs no permission on the form or table; only what the fill page shows is returned.
- Submit through the API only when `status.key` is `open` and `blockers` is empty; otherwise `status.message` says why, and a non-empty `blockers` means the page must be filled in a browser.
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

createFillFormEntry.summary: Submit an entry through a form's fill page
createFillFormEntry.description:
Submits one entry through the fill page as the current user, the same as clicking "Submit" on the page: only fields visible on the fill page are accepted, required fields are checked as the fill page sets them,
the submitter is recorded as the current user (the entry shows up in "My submissions"), and an entry submitted through a form view records which view it came from.
- Returns 403 when the fill page is not open, with the reason in `status`; returns 422 listing the reasons when `blockers` is not empty.
- Returns 422 when a field value is invalid, with `errors` explaining each by field api_code.
- Each user can submit at most 30 times per hour; beyond that returns 429.
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

getFillViewPage.summary: Show a form view's fill page
getFillViewPage.description:
Reads the fill page behind a fill link (`/v/<token>`): its title, description, the fields to fill in, and whether the current user can submit right now.
The caller reads it as a submitter holding the link and needs no permission on the form or table; only what the fill page shows is returned.
- Submit through the API only when `status.key` is `open` and `blockers` is empty; otherwise `status.message` says why, and a non-empty `blockers` means the page must be filled in a browser.
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

createFillViewEntry.summary: Submit an entry through a form view's fill page
createFillViewEntry.description:
Submits one entry through the fill page as the current user, the same as clicking "Submit" on the page: only fields visible on the fill page are accepted, required fields are checked as the fill page sets them,
the submitter is recorded as the current user (the entry shows up in "My submissions"), and an entry submitted through a form view records which view it came from.
- Returns 403 when the fill page is not open, with the reason in `status`; returns 422 listing the reasons when `blockers` is not empty.
- Returns 422 when a field value is invalid, with `errors` explaining each by field api_code.
- Each user can submit at most 30 times per hour; beyond that returns 429.
- An account access token has no "current user"; calling with one returns 400.

moveTableToFolder.summary: Move a table into a folder
moveTableToFolder.description:
Moves a table into a folder, or out of its folder (`folder_token` set to null); PUT is also accepted. The move affects only the calling user's folder placement.
- The request body must include the `folder_token` key (its value may be null); otherwise 400.
- `folder_token` accepts only a folder token (not an id); returns 404 when the folder does not exist or the current user lacks manage permission on it.
- The target folder's kind must be table; otherwise 400.
- Returns 404 `table cannot be found` when the token is not a table's.

listRoutines.description:
The current user's own routines, newest first.
- Paging: `next` is a row offset; pass it back unchanged for the next page. `skip` and `next` cannot be passed together. 50 per page by default, `limit` changes it (at most 1000).
- Routines belong to a person: a credential with no current user (an account access token and the like) returns `403`, and so does an account that cannot use routines yet.

createRoutine.description:
Creates a routine, enabled from the start. The rules and messages are those of the routines page: a name of at most 60 characters, an instruction of at most 2000, only forms, tables, views and query pages you can reach as objects, at most 20 enabled routines per person, and a one-off time later than now. A data trigger's source is added to the objects.
- A routine against the rules returns `422`, and `errors` gives each reason with its `code` and the page's message.
- Delete authorization (`delete_authorized`) cannot be set here: a body that names it, true or false, returns `422` `delete_authorization_page_only` and creates nothing.
- Jiri running a routine cannot create routines (`403`).

getRoutine.description: One of your own routines. Someone else's, or one that does not exist, returns `404`.

updateRoutine.description:
Changes the name, instruction, objects, trigger kind, schedule or data trigger. A key left out, or null, keeps what the routine has; `objects` given replaces them all.
- The rules and messages are those of creating. A changed schedule cancels the runs queued for the old one; a changed instruction or objects stops a run in progress.
- A body that names `delete_authorized`, true or false, returns `422` `delete_authorization_page_only` and changes nothing.
- Jiri running a routine cannot update routines (`403`).

deleteRoutine.description:
Deletes the routine for good: it never runs again, and its queued and running runs are cancelled. The conversations of its past runs stay.
- Jiri running a routine cannot delete routines (`403`).

pauseRoutine.description:
The routine stops running, and its queued and running runs are cancelled. Pausing a paused routine returns it as it is.
- Jiri running a routine cannot pause routines (`403`).

resumeRoutine.description:
Enables a paused routine, which runs again from its next time after now; times missed while it was paused are not made up. Resuming an enabled routine returns it as it is.
- As with creating, at most 20 routines can be enabled (`422` `active_limit`). A one-off whose time has passed returns `422` `once_passed`; a data trigger whose fields no longer work returns `422`.
- Jiri running a routine cannot resume routines (`403`).

runRoutine.description:
Queues one run now, paused routines included, and returns it. When it starts it is checked as a scheduled run is: AI points, the daily run limit, and access to the objects. Its outcome shows in the routine's runs.
- A run still in progress returns `422` `invalid`; so does a data trigger whose fields no longer work.
- Jiri running a routine cannot run routines (`403`).

listRoutineRuns.description: The runs of one of your own routines, latest planned time first. Paged as `GET /routines` is.
